properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The DEFAULT TSIG algorithm for RFC2136 DNS-01 updates — a weak default (digest-broken MD5, quantum-unsafe) that every rfc2136 user gets unless they explicitly set tsigAlgorithm. Changeable here: flip the default to HMACSHA256 and keep HMACMD5 opt-in for legacy BIND interop.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed PEM private keys (RSA-2048, EC, Ed25519) embedded as Go string constants in unit and e2e test fixtures — throwaway CA/issuer keys for the self-signed, CA and Vault issuer test suites. Real key material in source, but deliberately public test material that never protects production data; rotation is meaningless, so the D rating reflects exposure hygiene rather than a live secret.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Legacy TSIG interop algorithm (RFC 2845 hmac-md5.sig-alg.reg.int) user-selectable in the rfc2136 DNS-01 provider; weakest item in cert-manager's TSIG menu. Changeable here — removing HMAC-MD5 support is an interop decision for legacy BIND deployments.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RFC2136 DNS-01 TSIG algorithm menu offered to users via the rfc2136 provider config (also enumerated as CRD/openapi enum values). Changeable here — dropping HMAC-SHA1 support is an interop decision for the DNS providers in use.

properties.name: pqs:context

Quantum-unsafe under Shor; no PQ account-key path exists yet (ACME CAs don't offer PQ), so this is a PQ-migration blocker to track. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The HMAC-SHA1 option of the RFC2136 TSIG algorithm menu: exposed as CRD enum documentation and openapi description, admitted by the Issuer validation allowlist, mapped in rfc2136.go and implemented in tsig.go. Sound as a MAC but deprecated; quantum-unsafe. Changeable here by narrowing the supported tsigAlgorithm values.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Self-signed throwaway root CAs generated in code (x509.CreateCertificate with subject==issuer) across unit tests, the e2e Vault addon and the webhook test helper — scaffolding to exercise CA-issuer, Vault-issuer and webhook-serving code paths. Genuine self-signed cert generation, but never production trust material. The underlying signature algorithm (RSA-2048 in testwebhook.go per the AST chain, ECDSA elsewhere) is covered by the ECDSA/RSA objects.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared HMAC algorithm constants for the ACME external-account-binding (EAB) key: HS256/HS384/HS512 in the issuer API types (internal and its public mirror). The field is deprecated and inert — golang.org/x/crypto/acme hardcodes the EAB MAC to HMAC-SHA-256 (HS256) regardless, so the JOSE signature cert-manager produces at EAB registration is always HS256. Real protocol-configuration surface; HMAC-SHA-256 is Grover-attenuated rather than Shor-broken, making this a records item, not harvest-now-d

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PKCS#12 keystore encryption for the OPT-IN Modern2026 profile only: PBES2 AES-256-CBC + PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256, PBMAC1 HMAC-SHA256 integrity. The shipped DEFAULT profile is LegacyRC2 (RC2-CBC/3DES/SHA-1) — see the separate RC2 finding; the CBC-malleability concern here applies only to users who select Modern2023/2026.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-fixture credentials only; they are real hardcoded literals in the repository but grant access to nothing outside the local test harness. Changeable here (move to env/vault) if the repo wants a no-credentials-in-source policy, but no production exposure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA (P-256 default, P-384/P-521 selectable via keySize) is one of the three key algorithms cert-manager issues (RSA/ECDSA/Ed25519), covering generated private keys, CSR signature selection (ECDSAWithSHA256/384/512) and issued certificates; the webhook's dynamic TLS authority also uses ECDSA CAs in tests. Quantum-unsafe under Shor — migration is blocked on the X.509/PKI ecosystem adopting PQ signatures (ML-DSA/SLH-DSA certificates); changeable here only by narrowing the offered menu.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 (Curve25519, PureEd25519 signatures) is the third offered key algorithm for issued certificates; the strongest classical option cert-manager issues but still Shor-vulnerable. Migration is blocked on the X.509/PKI ecosystem adopting PQ signatures (ML-DSA/SLH-DSA certificates); changeable here only by narrowing the offered menu.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All outbound HTTPS sessions cert-manager opens (ACME account and protocol clients, Cloudflare DNS-01 API client, Venafi client, HTTP-01 solver, e2e Vault clients) plus the TLS server in pkg/server/listener.go use Go 1.27 crypto/tls defaults: X25519MLKEM768 is the first-preference group (hybrid PQ, negotiated by any capable peer), with SecP256r1MLKEM768/SecP384r1MLKEM1024 also offered and classical x25519/secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1 permitted as fallback — weakest group x25519 (B-). Harvest-now

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 (secp256r1) is the default curve for user-requested ECDSA private keys (spec.privateKey.algorithm: ECDSA, keySize 256) and for CSR signature selection. Quantum-unsafe under Shor; changeable here through the CRD keySize field and the defaults in pkg/util/pki.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Version bound in production: the Venafi TPP/Cloud client floors TLS at 1.2, so a TLS 1.2-only Venafi endpoint forces classical ECDHE key exchange (harvest-now-decrypt-later). Against 1.3 peers, Go 1.27 offers hybrid X25519MLKEM768 by default, so raising the floor to 1.3 is the PQ remediation. The other three sites (e2e Vault addon, webhook test server and its client) are test scaffolding with the same floor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The rootEd25519Key committed in test/e2e/suite/issuers/selfsigned/fixtures.go (PKCS#8 PEM, content-identified) — a throwaway Ed25519 root key for the selfsigned-issuer e2e suite, deliberately public test material. Its site is one of the 9 committed-key sites in ALG-394bd8ab (fixtures.go:85); kept as a distinct entry because it is an individually identified key, with ALG-394bd8ab as the group view. Ed25519 is Shor-vulnerable in principle, but a public test key has no confidentiality to break.

properties.name: pqs:context
